title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation of a generate–validate–repair (GVR) wrapper around a single LLM generator (declared gpt‑5‑mini) for intent→device‑configuration NetOps tasks. Using a shared‑initial paired design (preregistration cns‑m2026‑01) we tested 300 intents (600 episodes). Baseline generator proposals were execution‑validated correct in 299/300 tasks (99.667%); the guarded pipeline (deterministic validator ± ≤1 automated repair) produced 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.003333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Provider‑call accounting: 301 model calls (300 generator + 1 repair). All model calls, provider traces, validator traces, per‑episode scoring JSON, manifests, and hashes are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement. We present the preregistered design, deterministic scoring/validation semantics, full reconciliation accounting, diagnostic failure modes, operational implications, and reproducibility pointers.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being proposed to translate operator intent into low‑level device configurations. Production adoption requires reliable, safe outputs: a mistaken configuration can change reachability or violate policies. A widespread mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair) where a deterministic validator gates execution and, when necessary, requests repair. We measure the marginal effect of such a gate in a controlled, preregistered experiment. Our goals: (1) quantify the guarded pipeline's effect on execution‑validated correctness versus the generator alone; (2) archive full per‑call/provider/validator artifacts for deterministic reconciliation; (3) report statistically principled inference following the preregistration.
sections.related_work: Prior work explores LLMs for NetOps intent translation, verifier‑assisted synthesis, and generate–validate–repair patterns; representative leads include recent intent→config engineering and formal verifier integrations. Unlike prior prototype reports, we (i) preregistered a paired estimand (cns‑m2026‑01), (ii) froze repair budget and retry policy, (iii) used a deterministic emulator‑backed validator to operationalize safety as absence of unintended reachability/policy changes, and (iv) archived every provider and validator artifact with SHA‑256 hashes to enable bit‑exact reproduction.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as cns‑m2026‑01 (SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc...), which fixed the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, a shared‑initial paired design, repair budget ≤1 automated repair, exclusion/contamination rules, and the analysis plan (exact McNemar two‑sided; paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Task bank and selection. A deterministic task generator produced a 300‑intent corpus mixing filtered public examples and seeded synthetic templates; deterministic contamination heuristics excluded items flagged by exact or shingle overlap. The final manifest is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 91564bb6...).

Generator, validator, and guarded pipeline. Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e2...). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) parses candidate configurations, simulates device state transitions on an archived emulator snapshot, checks task constraints (allowed_touched_fields, group constraints, preserve_unspecified_state) and reports structured traces and a binary pass/fail. On validator failure the pipeline allowed at most one automated repair call (preregistered). All model calls and validator traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/scoring/ with SHA‑256s.

Shared‑initial semantics and accounting. To isolate the validator's marginal effect we used a shared‑initial candidate: the generator produced a single candidate per intent which served as the baseline output and the guarded pipeline input. This reduces generation variance across conditions and isolates gating/repair effects. Accounting of provider calls and cache usage is deterministic and archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256: f6da5050...).

Scoring and confirmatory test. Per episode outcome = 1 if the validator confirms the candidate yields an execution‑validated configuration that satisfies the intent and produces no unintended reachability/policy changes; otherwise 0. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided on paired discordant counts (n10,n01). We report the paired bootstrap percentile CI for the guarded−baseline difference (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The analysis implementation and seeds are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 7db06f53...).
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. Planned episodes: 600 (300 intents × shared initial). Completed: 600; failures: 0. Model calls used: 301 (300 generator + 1 repair). Raw outputs and logs archived: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 176776d1...), per‑episode scoring JSONs in execution/scoring/ (representative examples and SHAs cited below).

Aggregates and primary inference. Baseline successes = 299/300 (0.996667); guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: 3421adb5...): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Implementation and seeds archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 above) so readers may reproduce p and CI exactly.

Why p = 1.0. With small discordant counts (n10=1, n01=0), an exact two‑sided McNemar implementation that sums tail probabilities as or more extreme under the null can produce p=1.0; our analysis code and seed are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Users preferring alternative exact formulations or one‑sided tests can recompute from the archived contingency CSV.

Repair diagnostics. Repair calls: 1 automated repair was invoked (guarded) and succeeded; repair trace archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256: 4deb410d...). No guarded residual failures remained. Representative per‑episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/) include validator violation codes, parsed_command_count, and observed_touched_field_count; these are the basis for the failure‑mode taxonomy (archived). Table 1 and Figure 1 summarize counts and the single repair occurrence.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. In this controlled emulator corpus the generator already had near‑ceiling performance; the deterministic validator plus a single automated repair corrected the sole baseline failure at minimal extra model‑call cost (1 extra call total). For deployments where generators make more frequent errors or encounter adversarial/novel intents, the same gated pattern would likely yield larger absolute improvement but with commensurate verification and latency costs.

Construct validity notes. Our validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot; this is a conservative, reproducible proxy but omits certain production dynamics (hardware quirks, multi‑domain live interactions). The shared‑initial design isolates the gate effect (same candidate) but does not evaluate end‑to‑end pipelines that requery the LLM differently per condition; that design choice was preregistered to reduce variance and to provide a clean attribution of change to the validator+repair.

Statistical interpretation. The observed paired contingency produced a minute paired difference and an exact McNemar two‑sided p reported by our archived analysis executor; the high baseline success rate produces limited power to detect small differences (ceiling effect). The bootstrap CI bounds the paired difference at ≤1% in this corpus (95% CI upper = 0.01). We therefore present guarded improvement as evidence of the gate’s effectiveness in fixing a single isolated error under these controlled conditions, not as evidence of broad production gains across different task distributions or models.

Failure diagnostics and categories. Per‑episode scorer JSONs capture diagnostic codes (validator_violation_codes, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count). Across the corpus the single baseline failure was attributable to a generator omission that the repair call corrected; no validator false negatives were observed in the run. Detailed per‑episode JSONs are archived for audit and further subgroup analyses (execution/scoring/ folder).
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment (cns‑m2026‑01) the gated GVR pattern (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) corrected the single generator failure in a 300‑intent corpus at cost of one extra model call (301 total). Baseline 299/300 vs guarded 300/300; paired difference 0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, manifests, and hashes are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement to enable deterministic reproduction. The guarded GVR pattern fixed an isolated error at negligible extra cost in this controlled emulator corpus; extension to higher‑error, adversarial, or production task distributions remains future work but should apply the same preregistration and archival discipline to ensure traceability.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (archived references and runtime facts)

Initial master prompt (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: study_id = cns‑m2026‑01 (frozen plan) — preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7. The preregistration fixed the primary estimand, paired shared‑initial design, repair budget (≤1), retry policy, contamination/exclusion rules, and the exact analysis plan (exact McNemar two‑sided; paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729).

Declared model(s) and config: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider family: recorded in execution/provider_calls/ (full per‑call traces archived for every model invocation).

Orchestration and validation framework: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0) implemented to parse candidates, simulate deterministic device state transitions in an archived emulator snapshot, check task and group constraints, and deterministically return pass/fail with structured traces. Repair policy: a single automated repair attempt permitted on validator failure (preregistered). Representative repair trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba.

Primary run artifacts (representative):
- Raw run results: execution/raw_results.jsonl — SHA‑256: 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb.
- Task manifest (N=300): execution/task_manifest.jsonl — SHA‑256: 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990.
- Analysis log and exact analysis seeds/params: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256: 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e.
- Paired contingency CSV used for the confirmatory test: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv — SHA‑256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55.
- Deterministic reconciliation and provider call audit: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json — SHA‑256: f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6.
- Representative per‑episode artifacts (pair‑000001 example): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt — SHA‑256: 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json — SHA‑256: 2e4a1ef1389a18cfc5a0d6728d0978879c6675125b090b66c2dbd97b730ef153.

Run accounting and deviations. The execution manifest records: planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 301 (300 generator + 1 repair). All provider calls and call cache entries are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ with per‑file SHA‑256s (full manifest available). No manual, post‑lock edits were made to substantive manuscript content; all manuscript text describing run design and outcomes derives from the archived autonomous run artifacts.

Limitations (summary): single declared LLM (no multi‑model claim); deterministic emulator validator abstracts production dynamics and may not capture live multi‑domain behaviors; shared‑initial semantics isolates gate marginal effect but does not evaluate pipelines that requery the model independently per condition; repair budget limited to one automated attempt. See manuscript Limitations for full discussion.

I certify these artifact paths and SHA‑256 values are copied from the archived autonomous run and are not invented.
limitations: High baseline ceiling (baseline = 299/300) reduces statistical power to detect small practical effects; the run nevertheless reports exact paired counts and bootstrap CI.

Construct validity: the deterministic emulator validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot; production exposures (hardware variants, cross‑domain live interactions, asynchronous state) exceed this scope.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini); no claim of multi‑model generality.
Design semantics: shared‑initial design isolates the validator's marginal effect but does not evaluate pipelines that independently requery the LLM per condition.
Repair budget: only one automated repair attempt permitted; iterative multi‑call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
